Emma: Quick heads-up — I ran the end-to-end perf sweep for the priming (prefill) vs generation (decode) split. Unexpected hotspot: mixing phases in the same batch increases 95th latency by ~18% and causes KV cache miss rate to spike on long prompts.
Emma: Attached the flame + kv-hit-rate trace (summary below). Kernel selection oscillates between fast small-batch kernels and larger-matrix kernels which increases kernel launch overhead.
Omar: Can you paste the benchmark command and the exact perf numbers? Want to reproduce locally.
Emma: benchmark cmd: `./bench_runner --model redwood-v1-13b --seqs 32,128 --dist priming,gen --workers 8 --trials 30`
Emma: Summary: median latency stable, p95 +18%, throughput down ~12% when prefill+decode interleaved. KV miss rate jumps from 4% -> 22% for mixed-phase traffic.
Jia: Looks like KV cache thrash + kernel churn. Heatmap shows frequent kernel switches at token boundary where batch shapes change.
Jia: Also saw GPU SM utilization dip during handshake windows — small batches cause suboptimal kernel selection.
Ben: Two proposals: 1) hard-split queues per phase + separate batching policy and kernel affinity, 2) phase-aware scheduler that keeps a small reserved window for decode-heavy batches to avoid stealing priming tokens.
Ben: For (1) we should set token_budget targets: prefill_budget=1024 tokens, decode_budget=256 tokens (per-queue), with per-model overrides.
Omar: Curious about memory overhead of separate queues (more KV priming?). Any data on increased KV warmup cost?
Emma: Measured KV priming overhead: a cold priming run had ~3.2% extra token cost in first 5 tokens, stable after warmup. Tradeoff seems worth it vs p95 regressions.
SRE-bot: perf-regression-check: deploy/canary-2026-03-14 flagged service redwood-runtime latency surge in region us-west-2 (annotated). CI trace id: 0x7f3a2b.
Mike: I can run a canary with Ben's hard-split queue config. Suggest a gradual rollout: 1% -> 5% -> 25% with traffic mirroring to perf dashboard.
Mike: Example config I want to try (quick):
```
queue_policies:
  priming:
    token_budget: 1024
    max_batch_tokens: 8192
    kernel_affinity: small-batch-optimized
  decode:
    token_budget: 256
    max_batch_tokens: 4096
    kernel_affinity: streaming-optimized
scheduler:
  phase_awareness: true
  handshake_backoff_ms: 4
```
Karen: Two questions: 1) Does splitting prevent KV reuse between priming and gen if the same request re-enters? 2) How do fallbacks work when decode capacity is exhausted?
Jia: Good point — need a shared KV namespace with a priming-to-decode hint. On split: we keep the same KV handle but allow per-queue priming flags; we should prime decode-side from priming KV when possible to avoid double-copy.
Ben: Fallback plan: when decode queue saturated, route to an overflow queue with slightly relaxed latency SLO but higher batching to preserve throughput. Also add an adaptive token_budget that increases when decode queue depth is low.
Emma: Action items: 1) Mike run canary with Mike/Ben config and mirror traces (Mike). 2) Jia to prototype KV priming hint (Jia). 3) Omar reproduce locally and add microbench for kernel-switch cost (Omar). 4) Emma will add perf regression test to CI and baseline p95/kv-hit thresholds.
Omar: I'll try to get numbers by EOD.
Mike: Starting 1% canary now, will post dashboard link in this thread once available :rocket:
Karen: Great, thanks. If this stabilizes p95 we're good. Keep an eye on mem pressure and SM saturation.
Emma: Thanks all — ping me if you see strange kernel selection churn. Will follow-up with a short writeup and proposed rollout plan later today :eyes:
